ruleset_status: Dungeon-environment tables validated against Four Against Darkness Expanded Edition (2024). Play context (environment + terrain + weather flags) documented in play_context_table. Caverns/fungal grottoes environment routing, heroic/legendary skill tables (45/45 + 20/20 wired), class-trick implementation table (25 wired rows), and map-element structural validation (42 tiles) are on the home Rules tables panel; verify row text against owned PDF when available.

door_table.notes: Opened by spellcasting vs door L only. +1 Treasure in tile behind.
Lock-picked or destroyed by Lightning/Fireball; cannot be bashed.
Spend 3 Clues or illusionist spellcasting vs HCL.
Unlocked; opening triggers trap. Rogue may disarm vs trap L.
Opens with 1 Clue or 1 gnome Gadget point.

trap_table.notes: All PCs Save vs poison; barbarians and halflings add +L.
Lead PC Save; light armor -1, heavy -2, halfling/elf +1, rogue +L.

trap_table.result: The PC leading the Marching Order steps on a bear trap and must Save vs. HCL+3. Halflings and elves add +1. Rogues add +L. If the Save fails, the PC has a foot caught in the bear trap and loses 1 Life. The PC will Save at -2 vs. other bear traps or trapdoors and be at -1 to Attack and Defense rolls until that lost Life is recovered.
trap_table.notes: Lead PC Save; halfling/elf +1, rogue +L; failed save applies Bear Trap Wound until healed.

trap_table.result: Spears come out of a wall and attack 2 random PCs. PCs failing a Defense roll vs. a HCL+4 attack lose 1 Life.
trap_table.notes: Two random PCs Defense vs HCL+4.

trap_table.result: A giant stone falls on the PC in position 4 of the Marching Order. The PC must make a Defense roll vs. an HCL+4 attack or lose 2 Life. The bonus from armor applies, but the bonus from a shield does not.
trap_table.notes: Position 4 Defense vs HCL+4; armor applies, shield does not.

treasure_table.result: Dungeon/Caverns: 2d6 gp. Fungal Grottoes: choose 2d6 Food rations or 1 roll on the Rare Mushroom Table.
Dungeon: a scroll with a random wizard spell. Fungal Grottoes: choose a piece of bark with a random druid spell or 1 roll on the Rare Mushroom Table. Cavern: a prism with a random illusionist spell.
Dungeon: a jewel worth 2d6 x 5 gp. Fungal Grottoes: choose a gem worth 2d6 x 5 gp or 2 rolls on the Rare Mushroom Table. Cavern: a gem worth 3d6 x 5 gp.

Dungeon: a treasure chest with 3d6 x 10 gp. Fungal Grottoes: choose a gem worth 2d6 x 10 gp or 3 rolls on the Rare Mushroom Table. Cavern: choose a gem worth 3d6 x 10 gp or a prism with a random illusionist spell.

Dungeon: roll on the Dungeon Magic Treasure Table. Caverns: roll on the Caverns Special Item Table. Fungal Grottoes: choose roll on the Dungeon Magic Treasure Table or roll on the Fungal Grottoes Rare Item Table.

hidden_treasure_table.result: An alarm goes off, attracting Wandering Monsters!
The loot is protected by a trap.
hidden_treasure_table.notes: Rogue disarm Save vs HCL+1; otherwise random PC Save vs HCL+1 (2 Life on natural 1).

hidden_treasure_table.result: The treasure is protected by a ghost.
hidden_treasure_table.notes: Cleric ban Save vs HCL or all PCs lose 1 Life.

search_table.notes: Corridors Search at -1; a 0 counts as Wandering Monsters.
Choose hidden treasure, secret door, secret passage, or 1 Clue held by a selected character.

any.description: Treasure is protected by a trap.

corridor.description: The corridor is empty and may be searched.

room.description: This tile is empty and may be searched. Roll on the Special Feature Table for your environment.

any.description: This tile is empty and may be searched; alternatively, spend 2 Clues to find a Secret Passage.

corridor.description: The corridor is empty and may be searched.

room.description: Weird monsters lurk in this room.
This chamber is a dragon's lair.

wandering_monsters_table.result: Roll on the Weird Monsters Table.
Roll on the Boss Monsters Table.
wandering_monsters_table.notes: Reroll dragons and Foes never encountered as Wandering Monsters.

dungeon_special_events_table.result: A ghost passes through the party.
A Lady in White offers a Quest.
A wandering healer offers healing for 10gp per Life.
A wandering alchemist sells potions and poison.
dungeon_special_events_table.notes: If already met this adventure, roll on the Traps Table instead.

dungeon_special_features_table.result: Fountain/Pool: This is a source of fresh, clean water, and all living PCs can drink and clean their wounds. All PCs recover 1 Life the first time they encounter a fountain in an adventure. Further fountains have no effect. No effect on PCs who did not lose any Life so far in the adventure.

Blessed Temple/Shrine: A PC of your choice gains a +1 on Attack rolls against undead Foes or demons. As soon as the PC kills an undead or demon, no matter if a Minor or Major Foe, the bonus disappears.
Armory: All PCs can change their weapons if they want, within the limits of their class. All PCs who lost their weapons may pick up a new one.

Cursed Altar: An eerie glow emanates from a sinister altar. A random PC is cursed and has -1 on Defense rolls. To break the curse, the PC must slay a Major Foe alone, enter a Blessed Temple (see 2, above), or receive a Blessing.

Statue: You may leave it alone or touch it. If you touch it, roll d6. On a 1-3, it awakens and fights to the death (HCL+3 Artificial Boss Monster, Tier+5 Life, Tier damage, immune to poison, disease and all spells; if you defeat it, you find 3d6x10gp inside). On a 4-6, the statue breaks, you find 3d6x10gp inside but gain no XP from the encounter. A living statue is a Major Foe and may be the Final Boss (roll as usual to determine if it is a Final Boss) and it gives 1 XP roll. If it is a Final Boss, increase its Treasure to 100gp.

The tile contains a puzzle box. Roll d6 to determine its L. You may leave it alone or try to solve it with a Save vs. its L. For every failed attempt, the PC is hit by a blast of energy from the box (1 damage). Wizards and rogues add +L to this Save. If the puzzle is solved, the box opens: roll on the Treasure Table to determine its contents.

caverns_special_features_table.result: Stalactites. Mark stalactites on your map. During combat, an explosive Attack roll with a two-handed weapon has a 3-in-6 chance of causing a stalactite to fall. Roll d6: 1-3 it falls on a random PC, 4-6 it falls on a random Foe. The PC can avoid the stalactite with a successful Defense roll vs. HCL. If the Defense roll fails, the hero loses 1 Life. If the stalactite falls on a Foe, roll an Attack against that Foe with a bonus equal to HCL. On a success, the stalactite deals 1 damage to that Foe. The stalactite's Attack roll may explode (this represents multiple stalactites falling).
Stalagmites: Mark stalagmites on the tile. Stalagmites hinder movement. PCs can't explode Attack rolls in tiles with stalagmites.

Boulders: The tile is filled with boulders. Mark them on the map. PCs have +1 to Defense rolls vs. ranged attacks and -1 to Attack rolls with ranged weapons. Foes with a chance of surprise increase this chance by 1. PCs have +1 to Stealth Saves.

Echo: Mark an Echo on the tile. The shape of some rooms creates an echo effect that amplifies sounds. In tiles with Echo, PCs have -1 to Stealth Saves. Encounters with Wandering Monsters have a 2-in-6 (not 1-in-6) chance of occurring here. Spells and prayers cast have a chance of echoing. Every time a PC casts a spell or prayer, roll 1d6. On a 6, the PC can IMMEDIATELY cast the same spell a second time, for free, either on the same or on a different target.
Water Pools: A water pool may either have beneficial effects or be contaminated. Draw it on the tile with a blue marker. Whenever a PC dips into it, roll on the Water Pool Table below.

caverns_water_pool_table.result: Contaminated Water. The PC suffers -1 to all Saves until the end of the adventure or until Healing or Blessing is cast on the PC. The effects of multiple contaminations are NOT cumulative.
Water refreshes the PC and allows wounds to be cleansed. The PC heals 1 Life. Each PC can enjoy this effect only once per adventure.

dungeon_magic_treasure_table.result: Wand of Sleep, 3 charges. The user may spend 1 charge to cast Sleep. Only wizards, illusionists and elves may use it. Add +L to the spellcasting roll. Resale value: 30gp per remaining charge.

Ring of Teleportation. Allows the user to automatically pass a Defense roll, teleporting the PC out of the room. The PC may no longer take part in the current combat, but rejoins the party as soon as it ends. After 1 use, the ring loses its powers. Resale value: If unused, 50gp. If used, d6+1gp.

Fools' Gold. This pouch of magical but fake gold coins will let you automatically bribe the next Foe that asks for a bribe. No matter how much the Foe asks, the gold will be enough to satisfy its request. This is a one-use magic item. If unused, it can be resold for 20gp.

Magic Weapon. Gives +1 to Attack rolls. This is a permanent magic item. Roll d6 to determine its type: 1) crushing light weapon, 2) slashing light weapon, 3) crushing hand weapon, 4) slashing hand weapon, 5) slashing two-handed weapon, 6) bow with 12 arrows. Resale value: 100gp + 2x weapon's cost.

Potion of Healing. Can be imbibed at any moment, even during combat, as a free action, healing all lost Life to a single PC. This is a one-use magic item. No PC may drink more than 1 Potion of Healing per adventure. Resale value: 100gp.

Dungeon/caverns: Fireball Staff, 2 charges. Spending 1 charge allows the user to cast Fireball. Only wizards may use it. Add the PC's L to the spellcasting roll, as for a spell cast by that PC. Resale value: 60gp per charge remaining. Fungal Grottoes: roll on the Rare Mushroom Table.

minion_reaction_table.result: The minions try to take captives! Their attacks are non-lethal. This p.102 roll-1 rule overlays named Minion bestiary tables as well as the generic Minion table.

major_reaction_table.result: The foe demands a large bribe.
The foe fights to the death!

basic_spells_table.result: Removes curse or petrification from one ally (combat or exploration).
Teleports the caster to the first tile of the adventure. Works automatically; may be cast during combat or exploration instead of a Defense roll.
Lightning bolt vs. one foe: spell total must meet foe Level; slays 1 vermin/minion on hit, or 2 Life damage to a boss/weird foe. Some elementals are immune.
Area vs minions: on hit, slays max(1, spell total − minion Level) vermin/minions. Single boss/weird: 1 Life damage on hit (cannot also wipe minions). Dragons immune. Mummies +2 on the roll.
+1 Defense for one ally until combat ends.
Spellcasting roll vs. one foe; on hit, defeats one boss/weird or knocks out d6+L vermin/minions. No effect on undead, dragons, artificial/construct/elemental/spirit foes, or foes L11+.
Cleric prayer: restore d6+L Life to one ally. Three uses per adventure; stays on the spell list when expended.

druid_spells_table.result: Melee-style spellcasting vs vermin with +2×L; disperses (no loot) rather than slaying.
The druid summons a large animal (boar, large cat, bear) to fight for the party: a L3 beast ally with 5 Life that deals 1 damage per turn for the encounter.

Spellcasting roll vs target L. On hit choose one: inflict 2 damage to a fire-based creature/natural fire; disperse 2 Vermin; knock out 1 Minion; distract 1 Major Foe so the party can flee without being attacked. Also creates enough water for party, mounts, and hirelings for a full day. Cast at +1 near water, -2 in desert, no modifier in dungeons.
Transform into a bear (warrior L, 8 Life) until combat ends; half bear damage applies after.
Destroys wooden doors/objects or inflicts 2 damage to plant/wood foes.
+2 Defense until combat ends; -2 on agility Saves and vs fire.
Like Lightning but outdoors only (not in dungeons).
Auto-entangles one major or d6 minor foes (-1 effective L this encounter).
Like Spiderweb but only outdoors in forest/swamp/jungle.
All allies ignore the -1 subdual attack penalty until combat ends.
Woodland travel ignores vegetation for 10×L minutes (outdoors only).
Outdoor weather control; +1 to druid Lightning Strike, douses fires, etc.

illusionist_spells_table.result: +L Defense until combat ends (no bonus vs vermin/undead/artificial/elemental).
Creates L+1 images (1 Life each) that absorb one hit each.
Summons a servant to carry treasure (200gp, weapons, armor) until slain or trapped.
Dispels illusions/invisibility; invisible foes become visible at reduced L.
Spellcasting roll holds a foe for L turns (+2 to hit; subdual damage).
Mist suspends ranged/gaze attacks; +2 Defense when fleeing.
Disguise for L hours; reroll Reaction or social Save.
Subdual damage equal to spellcasting roll on hit.
Foes must pass Morale or cannot attack the illusionist this encounter.
Successful roll counts as an immediate successful Bribe Reaction.
Creates L+3 illusionary food rations (max 7 days sustenance).
Flaming sword +L Attack for L+3 turns; all damage is subdual.

scrolls_table.result: Spend 1 turn to read and cast the scroll spell; the scroll is destroyed.
Any PC except barbarians may burn a scroll.
Barbarians may not use magic items, scrolls, or potions; they may carry them for allies.
Non-casters add +1 to the spellcasting roll; casters add +L even if the spell is not memorized.
Wizards may copy a new spell into their spellbook instead of casting (destroys scroll).
Wizard spells on parchment; illusionist spells on prisms; druid spells on bark.

experience_classical_table.result: Earn 1 XP roll after 10 minor-foe encounters (vermin/minions; foe count per fight does not matter).
Earn 1 XP roll for each Secret revealed (3 Clues).
Earn 1 XP roll for each Major Foe defeated (weird or boss).
Earn 1 additional XP roll for the dungeon Final Boss; room major foes can be revealed by a scout, which rolls the Final Boss check immediately.

Spend an XP roll to advance. Basic heroes roll d6 > Level (6 always succeeds). Expert-trained heroes roll d8+2 and may choose Level up or Learn expert skill/spell. Expert tier entry is a separate 500gp or 1 banked-XP training cost.

economy_services_table.result: Restore 1 Life to one hero while the healer is on the current tile.
Potion of Healing added to one hero inventory (once per hero per adventure).
Blade poison added to one hero inventory (once per hero per adventure).

experience_slow_sure_table.result: At the end of a successful adventure, one surviving PC gains 1 Level (no XP rolls during play).

experience_old_school_table.result: Add defeated foe levels to XP tally (vermin: half levels, rounded down).
Add 1 XP per gp claimed (resale value for magic items).
Spend (Tier+2)×100 XP to gain 1 Level (same PC cannot level twice in a row unless sole survivor).

experience_slower_table.result: Earn XP like Classical, but bank points instead of immediate rolls.

Spend XP equal to target Level to attempt advancement; +1 per extra XP spent. Expert-trained heroes use Expert dice and may learn expert skills instead of leveling. Expert tier entry is paid separately through Tier training.

swashbuckler_traits_table.result: Once per combat, after a successful Attack, you may immediately make a second off-hand Attack without spending an action.
swashbuckler_traits_table.implementation: wired: combat ability flourishing_strike; bonus off-hand after main-hand hit

swashbuckler_traits_table.result: Once per adventure, you may disengage from melee without provoking an attack. The Foes are so surprised by your acrobatic escape that an ally gains a +1 to their next Attack roll against a Foe of your choice.
swashbuckler_traits_table.implementation: wired: flee (Daring Escape) skips parting blows; ally +1 vs chosen foe once/adventure

swashbuckler_traits_table.result: Once per combat, if an enemy misses you in melee, you may immediately counterattack with your off-hand weapon. This Attack roll happens in the Foes' turn, before the party's next turn begins.
swashbuckler_traits_table.implementation: wired: combat ability riposte; off-hand counter on successful melee Defense

swashbuckler_traits_table.result: Once per adventure, you may reroll a failed Defense roll at +1. If the reroll is a 1, your plumed/tricorn hat is destroyed. You must buy a replacement for 6gp when you visit a settlement. You may not use Pirate's Luck until you have a new hat. The hat is not magical but may be stolen by Invisible Gremlins.
swashbuckler_traits_table.implementation: wired: lucky_hat class ability on failed Defense; hat destroyed on natural 1

swashbuckler_traits_table.result: Once per combat, you may mock a Foe to distract them. The target suffers -Tier on its L on its next turn (L will not be reduced below 1). Taunt does not work on Weird Monsters, or on Unliving Foes, but it works on vampires.
swashbuckler_traits_table.implementation: wired: swashbuckler_taunt class ability; −Tier on foe next turn (vampires OK)

swashbuckler_traits_table.result: Once per adventure, you may spend any number of panache points to add a +1 bonus per point to your next Attack and Defense rolls. If the combat ends before you have a chance to perform the Defense roll, that bonus is lost and does not carry over.
swashbuckler_traits_table.implementation: wired: blade_dance class ability spends Panache; +1/point on next Attack and Defense

quest_table.result: Bring me its head! The Quest-giver asks you to kill a Boss Monster. Roll on any Boss Monster Table to select a target. The next time you meet a Boss, instead of rolling it, you may choose to encounter the Boss Monster from the Quest. Bringing its head to the Quest-giver's tile completes the Quest.
Bring me Gold! The Quest-giver asks you to bring d6x50gp worth of treasure to the Quest-giver's tile. If you already have that much treasure, double the amount required.
I want it alive! Subdue a Boss and bring it to the Quest-giver.
Bring me that! Find the quest item on a Major Foe (1-in-6 per kill).
Let peace be your way! Complete 3 non-violent encounters (bribe, peaceful reaction, Sleep).

Slay all the Foes! Defeat the Final Boss and clear all foes from the dungeon. On an infinite map, the dungeon must cover at least a 20x28 grid area and all known foes must be dead before the Epic reward can be claimed without returning to the Quest-giver.

epic_rewards_table.reward: The Book of Skalitos. This book belonged to the legendary wizard Skalitos. It counts as 1 scroll of each of the 6 basic wizard spells. You may tear up the pages and distribute the scrolls among the party, or leave the book as it is and assign it to a single PC. The book is destroyed if the carrier is killed by dragon breath. If unused, it may be sold for 650gp.
The Gold of Kerrak Dar: spend 1 Clue on Search to find 500gp.

Enchanted weapon. One of the party's weapons is enchanted. Roll 2 dice for its Attack rolls, choosing the best result. If both dice roll an Explosion, roll both Explosions and choose the best. The weapon can hit Foes hit only by magic. The enchantment lasts until the end of the adventure.

Shield of Warning. This magic shield's protection counts even if the user is surprised by Wandering Monsters, fleeing from a combat, or fighting Foes that ignore shields. This is a permanent magic item. Resale value: 200gp.

Arrow of slaying. This arrow will automatically inflict 3 damage upon a specific Foe. Roll on any Major Foe Table to determine which Foe is affected by it. The arrow may be used only by a PC with a bow. It strikes automatically against its designed target. Once used, the arrow breaks. If unused, it may be sold for 3d6x15gp.

Holy symbol of healing. A cleric using this symbol adds +2 to the Life points healed by the Healing prayer. If the PC dies and the symbol and the cleric's body are delivered to the cleric's temple, the church will pay for an attempt to resurrect the cleric. After the resurrection attempt, the holy symbol will remain with the church. Resale value: 700gp.

combat_notes: Attack: exploding d6 + modifiers; total >= foe L to hit (p.91-92).
Defense: exploding d6 + modifiers; total > foe L to avoid 1 damage; natural 1 always fails (p.96).
Light armor +1, heavy armor +2, shield +1; rogues add +L to Defense (p.96).
Minor foes: slain count = attack total // foe L (p.94).
Major foes: damage = multiples over L; L drops by 1 below half Life (p.94).
Morale: minor group at half or less rolls d6; 1-3 flee (p.94).
Poisonous foes: after a hit, Save vs poison or take 1 extra damage (p.96).
Blade poison: envenom a slashing melee weapon or missile for +1 Attack vs the first foe (immune foes ignore it; p.165).
Magic resistance (p.97): spell connect vs base L, then penetrate vs L+MR (+1 magic_resist, +1 caster, +1 dragon).
Subdual damage: optional; damage is normal but 0 Life means knocked out, not slain (p.99).
Bribes: pay gp and/or surrender weapons per foe; category tables are fallback when mixed foes appear (p.167-178).
Missile combat: opening volley in rooms (once per hero); rear rank (3-4) may shoot every round in corridors (p.90-91).
Weapon modifiers: two-handed melee +1, light weapons -1, crushing +1 vs skeletons, unarmed -2 (p.93).

combat_modifiers_table.result: Poison vial: envenom a slashing melee weapon or missile for +1 Attack vs the first foe fought, then consumed.
Poisonous foe: after dealing damage, target Save vs poison (barbarian/halfling +L) or take 1 extra damage.
Magic resistance: connect vs base L, then penetrate vs L+MR tiers (magic_resist +1, caster +1, dragon +1).
Each prepared spell/prayer may be cast once per adventure (Healing prayer: 3 uses). Expended spells stay on the sheet but cannot be recast until the dungeon ends.
Subdual attacks deal normal damage; at 0 Life the foe is subdued (not slain). Required for bring-alive Boss quests.
Bribe results may demand gp or weapons per foe (e.g. Goblins: 5gp or 1 weapon each). Mixed payment is allowed.
Rooms: one opening missile shot per hero before close combat (even if foes strike first). Corridors: rear rank (3-4) may use bow/sling each round over the front rank's heads.

Two-handed melee weapons +1 Attack; light weapons (dagger, sling, scimitar) -1; crushing weapons +1 vs skeletons/undead; clerics use full Level Attack vs undead; Blessed Temple/Shrine grants +1 Attack vs undead/demons until one is slain; unarmed -2.

Fallen heroes may be looted in combat (forfeit attack), carried out (carrier: rearguard, no Defense), left outside at entrance, resurrected for 1000gp (d6 ≤ Level; L6+ automatic; full Life), or laid to rest as permanently lost.

Each hero carries at most 200gp in the dungeon; treasure shares from capped heroes redistribute to living heroes with capacity. Excess roster gold stays as home bank gold outside. Starting class weapons and shields do not encumber; extra gear beyond that baseline applies −1 Defense and Saves. Up to 3 extra weapon slots (two-handed = 2) and 2 shields total may be carried.
Roster gold is treated as home bank gold outside the dungeon. While camped outside, living heroes may deposit carried gold or withdraw banked gold up to the 200gp dungeon carry cap.

While camped outside for recovery, or from a saved session, Regroup Party may swap one or more heroes and set marching order before re-entering. Fallen bodies, gear, explored map state, and tile state remain in the dungeon.

Trolls regain 1 Life after each foe melee phase unless wounded by fire, acid, lightning, or oil since the last tick. Fireball, Lightning/Lightning Strike, acid vials, and ignited lantern oil suppress regen (foe card: Regen blocked).

Flammable oil / lantern oil (10gp shop or caverns/fungal loot): combat splash vs regenerating foes, 1 Life, blocks regen. Acid vial (Fiendish loot or resale 15gp): combat throw, acid damage, blocks regen — not sold in the home shop catalog. Wolfsbane (10gp shop): combat throw vs lycanthropes for 2 Life. Berserker's Mushroom (15gp shop): eat in exploration for one rage attack next combat. Rare mushrooms (fungal grottoes p.159): eat in exploration from party sheet. Fungal rare items (p.161): Morel Crusher, Red Death, Xicthul's Cap thrown in combat; White Angel Mushrooms eaten in exploration.
Good lock-picks (+1 lockpick attempts). Crowbar (+1 bash on locked/stuck doors; any class with a crowbar may bash). Warriors and barbarians may bash without a crowbar.
Giant spider webs block fleeing until a torch is spent (party sheet) or Fireball burns the web. Light sources grant +2 Defense vs light-averse foes (Morlocks, cave goblins, drow).
Hidden pit trap: failed Save drops the lead hero into a pit (Trapped in pit). Climb out with party rope or another hero's help from the party sheet.

Map Fragment (caverns): once per adventure, preview the next unrevealed tile. Wand of Power (Fiendish): 2d3 charges; wizard declares charges before casting (+1 per charge). Enchanted Paint (Fiendish): create food rations, hand weapon, light/heavy armor, shield, or paint a door; 1-in-6 runs out on use. Fungal Rare Item Table (p.161): Leafsteel/gem choice, Xicthul's Cap, Red Death (damage or −1 Level at find), Adventurer's Dead Body gear, d6 White Angel Mushrooms, Morel Crusher.
Note default melee and missile weapons on the hero sheet; wield default at encounter start. Swap melee weapon in combat costs 1 turn (p.94).

After combat, treasure rolls use each defeated foe template's treasure_rolls field once per foe name on the tile (not per individual). Templates with no_treasure or no treasure_rolls field award no rolls. Mixed major+minor: only major types roll; minor treasure is suppressed (EE p.180).

Fiendish mixed major+minor (EE p.180): clearing both together grants 2 XP rolls (classical) and suppresses minor treasure rolls. Fiendish-tagged foes on the tile use fiendish_foes_treasure_table / fiendish_foes_magic_treasure_table.

Lurking Mantlebeast (Fiendish weird): 2-in-6 spot (4-in-6 with rogue). Turn Back retreats via entry passage without combat. Start Combat or failed spot triggers ceiling drop (L3 saves; pin or free strike). Never wandering.
After slaying Fiendish Chaos Lord, optional Free Slaves grants 1 Clue and immediately rolls Wandering Monsters; Decline skips both.

Wired Fiendish template hooks: Skeletal Demon skeleton reinforcements (1 per PC Life lost/round); Hobgoblin Leader rattleblade (3-in-6 blademasters per attack, once); Doppelganger mimic+confusion; Acid Cube engulf; Giant Toad death-burst poison; Possessed Dwarf d6 3+ revival once; Young Red Dragon fire breath; Stirge blood drain; Chaos Lord random powers; Chaos Slavers preset bear trap.

caverns_trap_table.result: A stalactite falls! A random PC must Save vs. HCL+2 Trap or lose 1 Life. All PCs Save at +1/2 L. Rogues add +L. Halflings add +1/2 and may reroll a failed Save.
caverns_trap_table.notes: All PCs Save at +1/2 L. Rogues add +L. Halflings add +1/2 and may reroll a failed Save.

caverns_trap_table.result: Rockslide. Loose stones are dislodged, sending a cascade of rocks down the tunnel. All PCs must Save vs. HCL+2 Trap or lose 1 Life. All PCs Save at +1/2 L. Rogues, gnomes and dwarves add +L. Halflings add +1/2 and may reroll a failed Save.
caverns_trap_table.notes: All PCs Save at +1/2 L. Rogues, gnomes and dwarves add +L. Halflings add +1/2 and may reroll a failed Save.

caverns_trap_table.result: Hidden Pit. The first PC in Marching Order must Save vs. HCL+1 Trap or fall into a pit, losing 1 Life. All PCs Save at +1/2 L. Rogues add +L. Halflings add +1/2 and may reroll a failed Save. The PC needs the help of another to climb out of the pit. If you spend 1 Clue, at the bottom of the pit you find a Secret Passage to the dungeon or fungal grottoes (choose).
caverns_trap_table.notes: Spend 1 Clue at the bottom to find a Secret Passage to the dungeon or fungal grottoes.

caverns_trap_table.result: Swinging Log Trap. A large wooden log, bound with vines, swings from the ceiling. All PCs must Save, in Marching Order (first, the PC at position 1, then the PC at position 2, and so on) vs. an HCL Trap. All PCs Save at +1/2 L. Rogues add +L. Halflings add +1/2L and may reroll a failed Save. The process stops when a PC fails to Save and loses 2 Life, or if all Save successfully.

Toxic Mushrooms. A random PC steps on a patch of mushrooms, releasing toxic spores. The PC must Save vs. HCL+1 poison or be at -1 on all Saves for 6 rooms (1 hour). All PCs Save at +1/2 L. Rogues and foresters add +L. Mushroom monks are immune. Halflings add +1/2 and may reroll a failed Save. If a mushroom PC leads the Marching Order (position 1), ignore this Trap.
caverns_trap_table.notes: Mushroom monks are immune. If a mushroom PC leads the Marching Order, ignore this Trap.

caverns_trap_table.result: Rolling Boulder. Choose if it comes from the back or from the front of the party. 1d3 PCs in Marching Order must Save vs. HCL+1 Trap or lose 2 Life each. All PCs Save at +1/2 L. Rogues add +L. Halflings add +1/2 and may reroll a failed Save. At the end of the process, the boulder rolls towards another opening (choose one on the tile) and gets stuck in it. That opening is now blocked and cannot be accessed.

fungal_grottoes_trap_table.result: Sleep spores. A random PC must Save vs. HCL Trap or release a cloud of spores that will put to sleep all PCs who fail a Save vs. HCL poison.
fungal_grottoes_trap_table.notes: Mushroom, artificial, undead, elemental PCs are immune. Halflings add +L. All other PCs add +1/2L. If all PCs fall asleep, the whole party dies.

fungal_grottoes_trap_table.result: Spore Cloud. A random PC must Save vs. HCL+1 Trap or step on a purple puffball, releasing its toxic spores. On a failure, the PC must Save vs. HCL+3 poison or lose 1 Life and start coughing, triggering a 1-in-6 chance of Wandering Monsters.
fungal_grottoes_trap_table.notes: Mushroom, artificial, undead, and elemental PCs are immune. Halflings and barbarians add +L. All other PCs add +1/2L.

fungal_grottoes_trap_table.result: Slime Patch. The PC leading the Marching Order must Save vs. HCL Trap or fall down. Roll a 1-in-6 chance of Wandering Monsters. If they come, the fallen PC will skip 1 turn as s/he struggles back to his/her feet.

Mycelium Snare. A random PC must Save vs. HCL+3 Trap. On a failure, an object in their hands (shield, weapon, lantern, etc., player's choice) is snatched by a bunch of fungal fibers dropping from the ceiling, never to be seen again.

Shrieking Mushroom. The PC leading the Marching Order has a 4-in-6 chance of disturbing a small mushroom that will shriek, causing Wandering Monsters to arrive. Reduce this chance by 2 if the PC is a halfling or forester (druid, ranger or any other outdoor class) and by 1 if it's a rogue.

Cordyceps Trap. A random PC must Save vs. HCL+3 poison or be infected with a mind-controlling fungus parasite and attack the ally with the fewest current Life points (the attacked PC must defend vs. the L of the controlled PC). The mind control effect will wear off after 6 turns or if a Blessing or Healing are used. An ally killed by the infected PC will rise as an undead Boss Monster (Tier+1 Life, L equal to the dead PC's L) and attack a random PC.
fungal_grottoes_trap_table.notes: All PCs Save at +1/2L vs. the infection. Halflings and barbarians Save at +L.

caverns_special_events_table.result: You encounter a cave goblin scout. If you pay 10gp, he warns you of danger. Your PCs cannot be surprised by any Foe, including Wandering Monsters, and have a +1 to all Saves until you exit the caverns. If you do not pay, the goblin shrugs and walks away.

You encounter d6 cavemen explorers looking for food. Give them 2 Food rations (for the whole group) or fight them. They are HCL+3 Minions armed with clubs, standard Morale, 1 Life, 1 attack per turn, no Treasure.

You encounter a morlock Spy. If you pay 5gp, the Morlock betrays his companions. After speaking with him, you cannot be surprised by any morlocks, even those encountered as Wandering Monsters, until you leave the caverns. If you don’t pay, he runs away grumbling insults.
Trap. Roll on the Cavern Trap Table.
If you have a dwarf in the party, you find a gem worth d6x10gp. To collect it, however, you must risk a 1-in-6 chance of Wandering Monsters. If there’s no dwarf, ignore this event.

You meet a dwarf miner. You may sell any gems found or buy up to d6 gems worth 25gp each. If you make any trade with the dwarf, the dwarf will reveal the contents of the next tile before you decide whether or not to enter.

fungal_grottoes_special_events_table.result: You encounter a halfling scout. If you pay 10gp, he warns you of danger. The PCs cannot be surprised by any Foe, including Wandering Monsters, and will have a +1 to all Saves until they exit the fungal grottoes. If you do not pay, the halfling bids you farewell and walks away.

You encounter d6+2 cavemen looking for mushrooms. Give them 4 Food rations or 1 rare mushroom or fight them. They are HCL+3 Minions armed with clubs, standard Morale, 1 Life, 1 attack per turn, no Treasure. If you feed them, they will show you a secret passage (in next tile) leading from the fungal grottoes to the caves.
Spore cloud. All living PCs, except mushroom monks, must Save vs. HCL poison or lose 2 Life. Halflings and barbarians add +L to this Save.
Trap. Roll on the Fungal Grottoes Trap Table and then on the Fungal Grottoes Rare Item Table.

If you have a mushroom monk in the party, you sense danger approaching through the mycelial network. You may automatically ignore the next Trap or Wandering Monsters encounter in the fungal grottoes. If you do not have a mushroom monk, ignore this event. The warning has no effect in other environments.

You meet a merchant. You can buy any item from the Equipment list, but all prices are 20% higher (round up). You can also sell gems or rare mushroom for their full resale value in gp. This event is unique. If you roll it again during the same adventure, count as 1, above.

caverns_special_item_table.result: Glittering Crystal. This gem glows like a lantern and can be worn around a PC’s neck with a leather string, freeing the use of one hand. Resale value: 25gp.

Map Fragment. At any time, you may use it to roll the contents of the next tile before entering it. You may use it only once. The map fragment has no value outside of the Caverns section of the current adventure. It is worth 30gp for purposes of the Bribe Reaction while in the Caverns.

Adventurer’s Dead Body. In addition to a pouch with d6 gems worth 10gp each, you find 1 item of your choice: Heavy Armor, Lantern, 2-handed Weapon, Bow, Crossbow, Scroll with Blessing, Scroll with a random spell, or Jar of chicken blood.
Miners’ Ointment. Use once to ignore Wandering Monsters or avoid invisible gremlins. Not magic. Resale value: 20gp if unused.
Miners’ Amulet. When worn by a PC in position 1, ignore 1 Trap within the caverns. One use per adventure. Resale value: 30gp.

fungal_grottoes_rare_item_table.result: Choose: 1 small gemstone (2d6+2gp) or 1 suit of leafsteel armor (+2 Defense, counts as Light armor, non-magical; discard after 3 adventures).

Xicthul’s Cap. This rare mushroom is infused with the powers of chaos and bears Xicthul’s Eye on its cap. It can be thrown to inflict d3 damage on a Foe. The damage is automatic. Throwing it requires 1 turn. The user takes 1 damage when it is thrown. Resale value: 60gp.
fungal_grottoes_rare_item_table.implementation: wired: combat throw via use_mushroom; automatic d3; thrower loses 1 Life

fungal_grottoes_rare_item_table.result: Red Death. This rare mushroom can be thrown at a living Foe, automatically inflicting 1 damage or reducing the Foe’s L by 1 (choose the effect when the mushroom is found). It has no effect on unliving foes. Throwing it requires 1 turn.
fungal_grottoes_rare_item_table.implementation: wired: fungal_red_death treasure choice; combat throw via use_mushroom

fungal_grottoes_rare_item_table.result: Adventurer’s Dead Body. In addition to a backpack with 1 rope, 2d6 Food rations and 2d6gp, you find 1 item of your choice: Heavy Armor, Lantern, 2-handed Weapon, Bow, Crossbow, Scroll with Blessing, or Scroll with a random spell.

Mushroom Gatherer’s Basket. You find d6 white angel mushrooms. Each can be eaten as a Food ration, causing the PC to heal 2 Life. They lose healing power at adventure end and can then be sold for 10gp each.
fungal_grottoes_rare_item_table.implementation: wired: roll_white_angel_mushrooms; eat in exploration; 10gp resale after adventure

fungal_grottoes_rare_item_table.result: Morel Crusher. When broken, this dried morel mushroom projects vivid hallucinations to frighten Foes. Single use. The user may cause a Morale roll at -1 (plus the Foe's Morale modifier, if any) in a Foe. Foes who never Test Morale, Foes who rolled a "fight to the death" Reaction, unliving Foes and those immune to poison are unaffected. Resale value: 40gp.
fungal_grottoes_rare_item_table.implementation: wired: combat break via use_mushroom; morale roll at -1

fungal_grottoes_rare_mushroom_table.result: Slumber Amanita. Resale value: 10gp. One use. A PC may use this mushroom to add +Tier bonus when casting the Sleep spell. The bonus applies also if the spell is cast from a scroll or an item, such as a Wand of Sleep. Using the mushroom requires only the action needed to cast the spell.

Puffball Smokebomb. Resale value: 5gp. One use. You may drop this mushroom as a free action. You do not need a free hand to do so. This allows the party to flee a combat encounter without receiving any attacks. Mushroom and artificial Foes are unaffected and attack normally.
Brown Cap Delight. Delicious and nutritious, this mushroom counts as 1 Food Ration when eaten and as 3 Rations if used for a bribe (if allowed by the Foe's Bribe Reaction). Resale value: 15gp.

Phoenix Mushroom. A living PC who eats this mushroom gains +1 to all Defense rolls and Saves for 30 minutes (3 tiles). At the end of this period, the user loses 1 Life. Commerce of phoenix is illegal in most towns. It can be resold for 15gp.

Purple Truffle. This is so rare that, when you find it, you must roll a 3-in-6 chance that what you found is not the real deal, but a similar mushroom of smaller value (1d6gp). Halflings may reroll this 3-in-6 chance. The real purple truffle can be sold for 6d6gp.
Healer's Chanterelle. This mushroom can be eaten to heal all damage on a PC; if not used, it loses its power at the end of the adventure.

clue_spends_table.result: Spend 3 held Clues deliberately to reveal a Secret. Clues are held by individual characters; choose the PC who discovers it, then the spend drains held Clues from that hero first and other holders if needed. The discoverer gains the campaign-mode Secret reward and chooses one Secret from the p.123 list. Future-use Secrets show timing prompts on sheets plus encounter/combat reminders when relevant.

On a Trade Information reaction, gain 25gp per held Clue without losing those Clues, and/or buy 1 Clue for 100gp. Bought Clues are assigned to an individual character and persist on that roster entry.
Spend 3 held Clues to open an illusion door without an illusionist spellcasting roll. The spend drains individual holders and updates the party total.
Spend 1 held Clue from an individual holder to operate a lever door mechanism.

Spend 3 held Clues for eligible spell learning where the class rules allow it. Prefer the learner's held Clues first, then other holders if needed. Wizard/elf expert spells use the existing expert spell catalog; Expert-trained L5+ druids use the druid spell table.

Spend 3 held Clues any time a hero is held captive by foes to locate the captive's hideout (Someone Has Been Imprisoned secret). A new lair (2d6×2d6 cave) is generated adjacent to the tile where Clues are spent, guarded by the same foe type at double their normal count. Captives are found there with d3 Life. Pay Level×10gp ransom instead of fighting if the foes' reaction allows.
Some quests/special discoveries may spend Clues directly, such as Kerrak Dar-style hoards.

secrets_table.timing: Declare when the chosen Major Foe is met.
secrets_table.result: Use Secret action targets one living Major Foe from the hero sheet or foe chip/menu; party Attack rolls against that foe get +2 for this combat.

secrets_table.timing: Declare when the foe is encountered.
secrets_table.result: Use Secret action ends an eligible non-vermin, non-Final-Boss encounter peacefully; no treasure or XP is gained.

secrets_table.timing: Apply in an empty non-entrance room.
Apply after entering a non-entrance room.
secrets_table.result: Roll magic treasure for the current environment, resolve generic magic weapons immediately, and add the result as claimable room treasure.

secrets_table.secret: True Name of a Spiritual Entity
secrets_table.timing: Choose angel or demon when used.
secrets_table.result: One angelic rescue/heal or demonic damage/kill effect.

secrets_table.timing: Spellcaster only; choose spell when applying.
secrets_table.result: Add a spell from any list/table and gain one temporary slot for it.

secrets_table.secret: Increase of Magical or Spiritual Power
secrets_table.timing: Cleric or spellcaster only; choose spell/prayer when applying.
secrets_table.result: Gain one permanent use of a specific spell or prayer.
Find a basic spell scroll; it is added to the discoverer's inventory if possible, otherwise left as claimable treasure. Existing Burn Scroll and wizard Copy Scroll actions handle use.

secrets_table.timing: Requires 2 defeated Major Foes and 50gp components.
secrets_table.result: Unlock a healing potion purchase option before each adventure.

secrets_table.timing: Declare when eligible foes test morale.
secrets_table.result: Use Secret action declares the effect; the next eligible vermin/minion morale test in this combat fails. Encounter/combat reminders call out the timing when an eligible group is present.

secrets_table.secret: Someone Will Pay Big Money for That
secrets_table.timing: Apply after carrying a valuable item out.
secrets_table.result: One jewel, gem, or jewelry item sells for triple value.

secrets_table.secret: Your Enemy Is in the Dungeon
secrets_table.timing: Declare when a Major Foe is met.
secrets_table.result: Choose a living Major Foe from the hero sheet or foe chip/menu, swap that foe for a chaos lord, and fight it at +1 Attack.

secrets_table.timing: Declare in a room guarded by Minions or a Boss.
secrets_table.result: Rescue an important NPC for a magic item plus treasure, or doubled current gp.

secrets_table.timing: Barbarian or dwarf only; persistent character trait.
Pay food costs while camped outside before re-entering the adventure.
secrets_table.result: Use Secret action consumes 1 Food ration and gives the hero +1 current/max Life for this adventure; roster persistence strips the temporary bonus.

secrets_table.timing: Spend 3 Clues any time a hero is held captive by foes.
secrets_table.result: Spend 3 Clues to locate the captive's hideout. The lair (2d6×2d6 cave) is generated adjacent to the tile where Clues are spent; guarded by the same foe type at double their normal count. Captives are found with d3 Life, stripped of equipment. Pay Level×10 gp ransom instead of fighting if the foes' reaction allows.

secrets_table.timing: Declare when chaos fanatics are met.
secrets_table.result: All heroes defend at +1 against chaos fanatics for this combat.

secrets_table.secret: I Know Where This Corridor Leads
secrets_table.timing: Use in exploration before the tile is resolved.
secrets_table.result: Reroll one room content table roll on the current tile; the reroll is final.

secrets_table.secret: I Can Cook This, and It's Yummy
secrets_table.timing: Requires a halfling in the party; use in exploration.
secrets_table.result: Halfling cooks rare ingredients; party +1 vs Madness, fear, and disease saves until leaving the dungeon.

items: Scroll/Bark/Prism with random spell OR non-magical weapon
fiendish_foes_treasure_table.result: Choose: 1 scroll, bark, or prism with a random spell, or 1 non-magical weapon of your choice. Roll a 2-in-6 chance that the weapon is silvered (+20gp resale, or +40gp if two-handed).
1 item of jewelry worth 2d6 x20 gp.
Roll on the Fiendish Foes Magic Treasure Table.

fiendish_foes_magic_treasure_table.result: Magic weapon. Roll d6: on 1-4 it has a +1 Attack bonus, on 5-6 a +2 bonus. Roll d6 for type: 1) slashing light hand weapon, 2) crushing hand weapon, 3-4) slashing hand weapon, 5) crushing two-handed weapon, 6) slashing two-handed weapon.

Magic armor. Roll d6: on 1-4 it has a +1 Defense bonus, on 5-6 a +2 bonus (permanent). Roll d6 for type: 1-2) shield, 3) light armor, 4-5) heavy armor, 6) ring of protection (usable by any class except barbarian).

1d3+1 vials. Roll d6 for each: 1-3) Healing Potion (heal all Life; one-use; max 1 per PC per adventure; not usable by barbarians; resale 100gp); 4-5) Acid Vial (throw as attack; roll d6, on 1 splashes thrower for 1 dmg, on 2+ inflicts 1 damage on a Foe; does not affect undead or golems; suppresses troll regen; resale 15gp); 6) Holy Water (1 damage vs undead per vial; barbarian exception applies).
Wand of Power, usable only by wizards, 2d3 charges. Each charge adds +1 to any spellcasting roll; declare how many charges before rolling. Resale value: 20gp per remaining charge.

Enchanted Paint. Whatever is drawn becomes real: a door on a wall (may connect two tiles), non-magical weapons, armor, equipment, or up to 8 Food rations (max 15gp value; no liquids). Each use: roll 1-in-6 chance the paint runs out. Resale value: 80gp.

Necklace with d6 prayer beads. A cleric may use 1 bead when performing a Prayer: roll d6, on 1-3 no extra effect (Prayer cast normally), on 4-6 the Prayer has its effect but is not expended. One bead is destroyed per roll regardless. Resale value: 15gp per bead.

play_context_table.result: Optional Fiendish Foes monster tables (EE p.180): enabled checkbox per adventure type (default on). When enabled and 2+ heroes are L3+, each monster table roll uses d6 1-3 standard / 4-6 fiendish. Traps, events, and special features still use the current environment tables. Only fiendish-tagged foes roll on Fiendish Foes treasure tables.

Mixed fiendish major+minor on one tile (EE p.180): defeat both together for 2 XP rolls; minor treasure suppressed; major treasure_rolls once per major type. See combat_modifiers_table fiendish_mixed_encounter and treasure_rolls_per_foe_type.

Template combat hooks in monster_combat_hooks.py: mantlebeast spot/Turn Back/ambush; skeletal demon reinforcements; hobgoblin rattleblade; doppelganger; acid cube; giant toad poison burst; possessed dwarf revival; chaos lord free slaves + wandering roll. Arrow of Slaying rolls any major foe table then picks a target (EE p.163).

Table-routing axis on session and tile: dungeon (default), caverns, or fungal_grottoes. Selects trap, treasure, special-event, and magic-loot tables. Secret passages can switch environment; does not by itself gate outdoor spells.
Default dungeon biome. Blocks outdoor-only druid spells (Lightning Strike, Alter Weather), Entangle, Forest Pathway, and ranger double bow/sling.

Surface/outdoor biome. Random-dungeon entrance tiles use outdoor terrain at the dungeon mouth. Enables Lightning Strike, Alter Weather, ranger double missile, druid companion wilderness entry, and paladin outdoor steed.
Woodland biomes on a tile: Entangle (forest, swamp, or jungle); Forest Pathway (forest or jungle). Set via map element editor terrain or imported adventure room terrain field.
Water terrains (pond, stream, river, lake, seashore, water) give Water Jet +1; desert gives Water Jet −2.
Session flag from Alter Weather (EE p.72): lasts until rest; −1 to party ranged attacks, +1 to druid Lightning Strike spellcasting.
Session flag from Forest Pathway (EE p.72): woodland travel ignores undergrowth for 10×L minutes (logged; cleared on rest).

Engine: resolve_play_context() in terrain.py combines tile environment + terrain with session weather/pathway flags. API enriches session.play_context on read; live map panel shows terrain and active flags.
